<!-- STEP -->
## Grow some roots

You can look at dividing cells yourself. Fill a jar with plain water and place an onion on it so that the base, which bears the roots, is in the water. Leave it for 5 to 6 days and watch the roots grow.

<!-- STEP -->
## Preserve the root tips

Cut 2 to 3 cm of the freshly grown roots and put them in freshly prepared aceto-alcohol for 24 hours. This is glacial acetic acid and ethanol, 1 part to 3 parts. Then move the roots to 70 per cent ethanol to preserve them.

**Your teacher or an adult should handle these chemicals.**

<!-- STEP -->
## Soften and stain

Wash a root and place it on a clean slide. One drop of dilute hydrochloric acid softens the tissue; rinse the root after 10 to 15 minutes. Add 2 to 3 drops of aceto-carmine stain and leave it for 5 to 10 minutes. Then warm it gently over a spirit lamp, with care, with your teacher or an adult beside you.

<!-- STEP -->
## Squash and look

Cut the tip of the root on the slide and put a coverslip on it. Press gently with your thumb to spread the cells. The slide is now ready for the microscope.
